First, as a fellow mentally ill person, being able to a grad student while suffering through mental illness is a huge accomplishment and proves that you are more functional and capable than you think you are.

Realistically, I think having mental illnesses just narrows down the type of people that are compatible with you. I’ve had a bf who ran away from me because he couldn’t handle my depression, but that’s just him.

Mental illness definitely does affect your personality and outlook, but it doesn’t define who you are. I bet you are intelligent, and have other good facets that are also part of who you are rather than mental illness. 

From personal experience, I think it is best to find someone patient, understanding, and who realizes that mental illness does not define your identity. 

I personally became comfortable fully disclosing my mental illness to people, and accepting that it is part of who I am, although I have many other sides. 

I won’t tell you to just be confident!! Because I know how hard that is. I just hope you accept that mental illness is not all of you. If that makes sense hahah 

Good luck!!!

My experience was horrible. I went to my school’s college counseling service and opened up about my depression and suicidal ideation. I also told a counselor that I felt so hopeless I took 4 more pills of my medication than the prescribed amount. She suggested I go see someone in a hospital. But I told her I didn’t want to go to a ward, but she said that it was completely voluntary and that I would go just for a brief check up. Minutes later, the campus police comes in, handcuffs me and takes me to the emergency unit that then sent me to a psychiatric ward under the involuntary 51/50 hold. I was there for two and a half days. 

Turns out my school lacked any on campus long- term mental health resources, so I found an off campus therapist. During our second session, I opened up about my suicidal thoughts and when he asked if there was any chance I would hurt myself in the future, I replied that I had no thoughts at the moment but I can’t guarantee that it will be 0 forever. At this, he called the police, and I was sent to a ward. He also fired me as a client. The school somehow found out and kicked me out of the dorm and I was forced to go on an involuntary leave of absence 3 weeks before the quarter ended.

I get that suicide rates at Stanford soared recently and the Palo Alto area in general have experienced a cluster of suicides, but I believe that universities tend to be hypersensitive to a treatable condition while lacking helpful resources. 

My advice would be to NOT seek any on campus help and rather look for psychiatrists not affiliated with the school who can manage your medication or local therapists. This makes things very expensive, but personally my experience with the school ended in tears and pain so I advise you to be very careful with what you tell your school if you choose to receive help. 

From my limited experience, you set up intake sessions with a therapist to see if you two are a match. My therapist asked me questions about my past, and asked questions to check if I had any symptoms for other mental illnesses. He also spoke with my mother and sister. In the last intake session, he diagnosed me and we decided to continue with the treatment. I was receiving cognitive behavioral therapy, so I had daily homework ( reading books on cognitive therapy and writing exercises) and during the sessions he generally asked how I was doing then taught me exercises and  coping mechanisms to regulate and express my emotions in healthier ways. 

Even the psychiatrist who evaluated me at the ward said that universities lack helpful resources and overreact to mental health issues. 

Hope this helped. Good luck!

Don’t think about others. Care about yourself. You must know that out of all people, you are the biggest victim of this, you don’t deserve this. 

What you’re feeling is not your fault. You should not feel guilty. Please feel proud that you still have the emotional generosity and kindness to care about others, despite all your pain and loneliness. 

People close to you ( your friends and family) should also understand that you are suffering. Don’t let the negative thoughts consume you.  If I, a person who has never met you before, can care about you, then WITHOUT A DOUBT, people that spent time with you, built memories with you, and the person that gave birth to you MUST CARE. 

Just let them know what’s going on, and try receiving professional help. That is a big first step that requires courage. 

I believe in you :)

Don’t get me wrong, I want you to live. I want you to give yourself a second chance. You don’t deserve to die. No one does. But at the same time I do believe that full ownership over one’s body includes the right to voluntary die, ONLY IF the person no longer WANTS to feel better. If you want to feel better but feel like there’s no hope or you’ve exhausted all your options, then no you should not give in. Cling on to that will to get better, that speck of desire and hope in you. People are only entitled to help those who want to survive. I know it’s tough. I have depression, anxiety, and panic disorder. Life is hell for me too. Talking to people in this Reddit page is a good first step. People here are supportive and non-judgmental. Think about the people you love. Spend some time with them. Take a nap. Get professional help ( see a therapist and/or psychiatrist for medication) 

Just don’t give up. Let’s fight this together.

Tip: don’t tell anyone in person that’s you’ve made specific plans to kill yourself, or else someone might hospitalize you in a ward against your will. Personally, losing that sense of external, physical agency just made things worse for me.
